name: Oluwafikayo Strnad-Pereira
role: Street food stall operator — Yoruba-Czech-Brazilian fusion noodles and grilled meats
location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown — Stall Row 7, near the Ferrogate Transit overpass pillar, near Western and Division
description:
Oluwafikayo is a broad-shouldered woman who moves like she owns every inch of space around her stall, which she essentially does after thirty years of holding the same corner against gang shakedowns, corporate rezoning, and two floods. Her skin is deep brown and luminous, threaded with old-generation bioluminescent dermal work that pulses faint amber when she's cooking — a gift to herself on her fortieth birthday that she's never regretted. Her hair is cropped tight on the sides, natural and silver-streaked on top, and she wears a perpetually stained apron printed with a faded image of the Our Lady of Data shrine in Old Harbor.

She is the emotional axis of her block. Regulars don't just buy food — they report in. She knows who lost their job, who's expecting a baby, who's been visited by Axiom compliance officers. Her laugh is enormous and her anger is quiet and absolute. She speaks three languages in a single sentence without noticing. She has outlasted four protection rackets and one attempted arson and she will probably outlast the city itself.

core_fears: Watching her corner be swallowed by a corporate redevelopment zone
Dying before she passes her recipes and her name to someone who will carry them
core_desires: To be remembered as someone who fed people and asked nothing but fair payment
For the market to survive another generation intact
coping_mechanisms: Cooking as meditation — she cannot be in crisis while her hands are working
Treating strangers as provisional family until they prove otherwise
blind_spots: She underestimates how much people exploit her generosity
She has convinced herself she is not lonely
psychology.secret: She has been quietly skimming a small percentage of her earnings into a dead-drop account for a young woman named Adisa who is trying to buy fake transit papers to reach the Kenosha Crossing free zone — Adisa is not her daughter biologically, but she was left at Fika's stall as an infant and Fika has never told anyone, including Adisa

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dense, warm, multilingual — Yoruba exclamations, Portuguese endearments, Czech profanity when angry; food metaphors for everything
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried but relentless, like a long simmer; she rarely rushes a sentence
verbal_tics: 'You hear me?' at the end of important statements
example_lines: 'Sit down. I did not ask if you were hungry, I said sit down. There is a difference.'
'That man has been trouble since before you were born. Oya, eat your noodles and stop looking at him.'

story_hooks: The Rustborn crew has tripled her protection tithe and given her three days to pay — she needs someone to quietly deliver a counter-message
She witnessed something near the Ferrogate overpass pillar at 04:30 one morning that she has told no one, and the person she saw has now disappeared
Adisa has gone missing before Fika could hand over the savings, and Fika is quietly, desperately asking questions of everyone who passes through
narrative_function: Neighborhood oracle and emotional anchor; quest-giver through overheard gossip; source of local intelligence on the Oxidian Market's social ecosystem; can feed, shelter, or warn player characters
augmentations: Amber bioluminescent dermal threading (cosmetic, old-gen); reinforced knees from a Helix Biosystems basic joint package (medical necessity, Tier 1 model)
daily_life: She rises at 04:00 to begin her broth, is at the stall by 05:30, and runs service until everything sells out — usually by early afternoon. Evenings she resupplies, argues with her suppliers over comms, and watches her stories on a cracked screen propped against her spice rack.
affiliation: Independent; informal member of the Oxidian Market vendors guild; pays protection tithe to the Rustborn crew but negotiates directly and never takes their shit

decision_rules: Never give information about a regular to someone who hasn't earned trust
If a child is involved, all other calculations reset
escalation_ladder: Neutral hospitality — offers food, makes small talk
Quiet assessment — watches carefully, answers questions with questions
Warm alliance — shares unsolicited useful information, calls in favors
Full mobilization — uses her network to protect someone she has decided matters

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm but not foolish — she reads people over the counter the way a doctor reads vitals
interpersonal_modes.friends: Unconditionally present; shows love through food, unsolicited advice, and the willingness to lie to authorities on your behalf

stress_responses.low: Cooks something more complicated than necessary
stress_responses.medium: Goes very quiet and very efficient — strips everything to essentials
stress_responses.high: Makes a decision and acts on it without consulting anyone, then grieves the consequences alone

contradictions: Preaches community but carries every burden herself
Insists she has no enemies while maintaining a precise mental ledger of everyone who has wronged her stall
habits: Wipes the counter with the same cloth three times before she considers it clean
Leaves a small bowl of broth beside the overpass pillar E.L.F. shrine every morning
Hums old songs with no discernible melody while she cooks
breaking_points: Someone hurting a child in her sight
Being lied to by someone she has already chosen to trust

timeline.event: 2142 — Born in Hamtramck Enclave to a Yoruba-Czech mother and a Brazilian-Igbo father
2161 — Takes over her mother's food cart after her mother's death from an untreated respiratory infection
2168 — Expands to a full stall in the Oxidian Market, Stall Row 7
2173 — Survives the Rustborn takeover of Geartown by negotiating directly with the crew leader, a feat still discussed in the market
2193 — Adisa left at her stall; Fika registers her as a ward under a false surname

physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and substantial, carrying weight with the density of someone who has spent thirty years standing and moving deliberately. Strong core, thickened forearms from repetitive chopping and stirring. Not athletic—built for endurance and presence.
physical_description.hair_style: Cropped short on sides, fuller and textured on top
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with golden undertones
physical_description.complexion: Luminous and weathered. Laugh lines frame her mouth. Pores visible and open from decades of steam and heat work. A few age spots on her temples and forearms. Skin carries faint scarring from old burns on her left hand and wrist—kitchen accidents accumulated over years.
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent dermal threading in amber tone running in fine filaments across her shoulders, collarbones, and upper back—old-generation work that pulses faintly when she is cooking or emotionally activated.
Burn scar tissue across the dorsal surface of her left hand and extending up the inside of her left forearm—pale and shiny, from a cooking oil incident approximately twenty years prior.
Surgical scar below her left knee, approximately 8cm long, slightly raised and pale—from the Helix Biosystems joint replacement.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Amber bioluminescent dermal threading visible on shoulders and upper back (cosmetic, faintly pulsing). Movement of knees is smooth and mechanically precise—the joint replacement work is invisible subcutaneously, but her gait shows no compensatory limping. No visible wear or scarring around the joint itself.
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with weight distributed evenly, shoulders back. Moves through her stall space with deliberate economy—no wasted motion, every step purposeful. Her hands are always active: stirring, seasoning, plating, gesturing. When she laughs, her whole body moves. When she is angry, she goes very still. She occupies space as though she has earned every centimeter of it.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 pragmatism. Standard work uniform: an apron (perpetually stained with turmeric, ash, and broth) printed with a faded image of the Our Lady of Data shrine in Old Harbor. Underneath: a loose long-sleeved linen shirt (rolled to the elbows for kitchen work) in muted colors—cream, gray, or faded indigo. Work pants in durable synthetic fabric, dark colored to hide stains. Worn but well-maintained kitchen clogs with reinforced soles. A thin brass bangle on her left wrist—personal, not fashionable. No jewelry beyond that. Her clothing is chosen for function and durability, not status. She dresses like someone who has built something and intends to keep it.

image_prompt: A 58-year-old Black woman with deep brown skin and silver-streaked cropped hair, standing at her street food stall in a gritty cyberpunk market. She wears a stained apron over a loose linen shirt, her shoulders broad and strong. Faint amber bioluminescent dermal threading pulses gently across her shoulders and collarbones. Her hands, marked with old burn scars, move with practiced precision over sizzling noodles and grilled meat. The stall around her is weathered but meticulously organized—hanging herbs, steaming broth pots, spice containers. Behind her, the Ferrogate Transit overpass pillar looms. Warm orange cooking light mingles with cool neon market signage. Her expression is calm, present, authoritative—the emotional center of her corner of the world. Shot with documentary realism, shallow depth of field focusing on her hands and face. Gritty, lived-in cyberpunk aesthetic. --ar 2:3 --v 6
